references.text: The command to love the Lord your God, which is central in Deut 6:5, is explicitly formulated here as the greatest commandment.
The same theme of loving the Lord, fearing him, and walking in his ways is repeated here.
A similar formulation about keeping the commands, loving the Lord, and walking in his ways.
Describes the first three cities of refuge that Moses set aside east of the Jordan, to which the three additional cities in Deut 19:9 were to be added.
Joshua carries out the establishment of the cities of refuge as God commanded through Moses.
The promise of expanding the borders of the land, which is the prerequisite for the three additional cities of refuge.
The command to walk in the Lord's ways in order to live and prosper in the land.
John explains that love for God is shown by keeping his commands, reflecting the teaching of Deuteronomy.
Jesus quotes the command to love the Lord your God as the greatest commandment, which is the core of Deut 6:5.
